params.body:
`www.sportbusinessgame.eu` answers 301 to the apex, and that redirect comes from nginx before any application: **one** header on the hop, **all four** on the page behind it. The exposure scan reads the hop, so a site that had just done everything right looked like a site that had done nothing, and the judge would have called a true claim false (the second way to make that mistake today; the first was elixir#199).

The header read follows a redirect now: at most three hops, and never off this registrable domain (www or not) because a redirect elsewhere is another site's answer. The probes keep following nothing, on purpose: there a redirect **is** the answer, and following it would let another page's content count as a find.

Tests: the headers behind a same-site redirect are the ones read; a redirect to another site is not followed. 652 green, PHPStan, Pint.
params.title: The headers read are those of the page a visitor gets
